title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page opens §45, a 'new recapitulation' of notation for automorphisms 'à lacets', i.e. inertia-preserving automorphisms.

Setting. Let π̂_{0,3} be the profinite fundamental group of P^1−{0,1,∞}, a free profinite group on two generators. It has inertia generators ξ_0, ξ_1, ξ_∞. Let Ŝ^+_{0,3} be the profinite completion of the orbifold group of P^1−{0,1,∞} modulo S_3. This is the extension 1→π̂_{0,3}→Ŝ^+_{0,3}→S_3→1. Grothendieck identifies it with SL(2,Z)^ (primed, really PSL(2,Z)^): the image of Γ(2) in PSL(2,Z) is free of rank 2 with quotient S_3.

(1) M̃_{0,3} is the group of automorphisms u of Ŝ^+_{0,3} such that:
- u stabilises π̂_{0,3};
- u respects the loop structure: u(ξ_i) = int(f_i)(ξ_i^μ) for i∈{0,1,∞} and a single μ∈Ẑ^*.
The f_i can then be taken in π̂_{0,3}, and are determined modulo the inertia subgroup on the left.
Restriction to π̂_{0,3} is claimed to be an isomorphism onto the inertia-preserving automorphisms of π̂_{0,3} that commute, as outer automorphisms, with the natural outer S_3-action.

NB (marginal). M̃_{0,3} is also the normaliser of Ŝ^+_{0,3} inside the big group Ŝ̂_{0,3} of all loop-automorphisms (Ŝ̂_{0,3} is glossed in the image as 'tous les autom. à lacets de π̂_{0,3}'). Equivalently it is a normaliser of π̂_{0,3}, identified with T̃_{0,3}.

(2)-(3) There is an extension 1→π̂→M̃→Ñ→1. Here Ñ_{0,3} = M̃/π̂ is the group of outer inertia-preserving automorphisms of π̂_{0,3} commuting with S_3.

(4)-(6) Since S_3 is complete, S_3 ≅ Aut(S_3). So the action of M̃ on S_3 = Ŝ^+/π̂ gives a homomorphism M̃→S_3. This equals the composite M̃ ⊂ Ŝ̂ → S_3, the action on the conjugacy classes of loops.

The next page factors this through Ñ and defines the kernels M̃^!, Ñ^!. It gets a canonical splitting Ñ ≅ S_3 × Ñ^!, and embeds the extended Teichmüller group T_{0,3} ≅ S_3×Z/2 (τ = complex conjugation).

Purpose. This is the genus-0, n=3 level of a Galois–Teichmüller formalism. Ñ^!_{0,3} is the group of outer inertia-preserving automorphisms of F̂_2 commuting with the S_3-symmetries. In modern terms this is essentially the group cut out by Drinfeld's 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations (I),(II), plus μ, without the pentagon. G_Q maps into it via the Belyi/Ihara representation.
errors: Writing SL(2,Z)^ for the extension of S_3 by π̂_{0,3} is loose. Literally it should be PSL(2,Z)^; the prime/accent in the manuscript probably signals this.
The loop-structure condition as transcribed (int(f_i')) is ambiguous. Presumably it is int(f_i)(ξ_i^μ) with one common μ for the three i; the manuscript is slightly unclear.

The restriction isomorphism requires injectivity, i.e. trivial centraliser of π̂_{0,3} in Ŝ^+_{0,3}, and surjectivity, i.e. extension of outer-commuting automorphisms. Both are true but not justified on the page.

ideas.what: Inertia-preserving ('à lacets') automorphisms of π̂_{0,3} commuting with the S_3 outer action, as automorphisms of PSL(2,Z)^ normalising Γ(2)^
ideas.modern_name: Inertia-preserving outer automorphisms of F̂_2 / pre-GT group defined by relations (I),(II) (Ihara, Drinfeld, Lochak–Schneps 'Out^#')
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981) discusses automorphismes à lacets and the équation des lacets; Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower)

ideas.what: Extension 1→π̂→M̃→Ñ→1, map to S_3 via S_3≅Aut(S_3), canonical splitting Ñ≅S_3×Ñ^!
ideas.modern_name: Splitting of the S_3-symmetry off the GT-type group at level n=3
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in GT literature (Drinfeld, Ihara, Schneps)

ideas.what: M̃_{0,3} as a normaliser of Ŝ^+_{0,3} inside the group of all loop-automorphisms
ideas.modern_name: GT as normaliser/automorphisms of profinite genus-zero mapping class groups (Harbater–Schneps description)

missed.claim: This page records an unpublished, systematic setup of the n=3 Galois–Teichmüller group. It is defined as loop-automorphisms of PSL(2,Z)^ normalising π̂_{0,3}, with its normaliser description and the splitting off of S_3. It anticipates the formalism of Ihara/Drinfeld/Lochak–Schneps but adds no result beyond it.
missed.quote: groupe des autom à lacets de π̂_{0,3} qui commutent extérieurement à l'action extérieure naturelle de S_3
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents how far Grothendieck took the GT-type formalism (with complex conjugation τ and the M̃/Ñ distinction) before Drinfeld's 1990 paper.

deep.surprise_reason: Definitional recapitulation of objects now standard in Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory, already sketched in La Longue Marche. It is historically nice, but contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: 'qui invariant π̂_{0,3}' should read 'qui invarient π̂_{0,3}', i.e. stabilise it.
'SL(2,Z)^{∧'}' in (1) is likely meant as the primed/projective version (PSL).
The marginal NB reads roughly: 'M̃_{0,3} est aussi le normalisateur de Ŝ^{+}_{0,3} dans Ŝ̂_{0,3}, et le normalisateur de π̂_{0,3} dans [Ñ_{0,3}] = T̃_{0,3}'. The final words are uncertain.
The gloss under Ŝ̂_{0,3} in (6) reads 'tous les autom. à lacets de π̂_{0,3}'.
